# Kalahavivāda Sutta (Snp 4.11 (PTS Snp 168))
**ID:** Snp 4.11 (PTS Snp 168)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kalahavivāda Sutta* (Snp 4.11, verses 862–877) is the eleventh discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇananda 1971; Tournier et al. 2014]. Framed as a dialogue in which an interlocutor questions the Buddha on the root causes of conflict and the nature of spiritual cessation, the sutta traces contentions, disputes, lamentation, and selfishness back through a dialectical sequence of conditions (*nidāna*), terminating in sensory perception (*saññā*) and mental proliferation (*papañca-saṅkhā*) [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇananda 1971; Watanabe 1983]. Modern scholars frequently highlight its analysis of societal discord as an early subjective formulation of dependent arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*), drawing parallels to the *Mahānidāna Sutta* [Bodhi 1984; Watanabe 1983; Shulman 2014]. According to commentarial tradition (*Paramatthajotikā*) and northern parallels, the dialogue was delivered with a magically created double of the Buddha acting as the interlocutor [Tournier et al. 2014]. The *Therīgāthā* commentary records that hearing this discourse moved Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī to seek ordination [Ohnuma 2012], while in Burmese liturgical practice, it was incorporated into expanded recensions of the *Catubhāṇavārapāḷi* [Kalupahana 2001].
A Chinese parallel survives in the *Arthapada-sūtra* (T 198, 佛說義足經), and the sutta corresponds to Arthavargīya No. 10 of the Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition cited by Śamathadeva [SuttaCentral; Tournier et al. 2014]. In the Pali canon, the discourse is exegetically unpacked verse by verse in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 11), with which DharmaNexus confirms massive verbatim overlap (87 matches across 8,000 characters), as well as further internal reuse in the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 8) and commentarial corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns several verse segments with the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D4099, D0326) [DharmaNexus].
